claim: A pilot with gpt-4.1-nano on 45 synthetic vignettes x 3 prompt variants (135 trials) gives accuracy 93.5%, mean confidence 78.4%, AUROC2 0.876, using a psychophysics-inspired metacognitive-sensitivity framework.
stance_target: F: psychophysics/signal-detection (type-2 AUROC) instruments applied to LLM confidence in a non-code domain
scope_conditions: single model pilot, medical vignettes, abstract
quoted_support: Across forced-choice trials, diagnostic accuracy was 93.5%, mean confidence was 78.4%, and AUROC2 was 0.876.

breadth.benchmarks: 45 synthetic AT-NCD vs DRCI vignettes; no code

claim: Exploratory GPT-family comparison suggests newer or nominally stronger models did not necessarily show better confidence-correctness discrimination; authors argue confidence should be measured directly rather than inferred from accuracy.
stance_target: F: capability does not imply confidence quality
quoted_support: Exploratory comparison across GPT-family models suggested that newer or nominally stronger models did not necessarily show better confidence-correctness discrimination.
